papers.title: From Inaudible Inputs to Model Failures: Low-Frequency Safety Risks in LALMs

summary.tldr: Researchers developed Intermittent Low-Frequency Lockout (ILL), an inaudible black-box attack using low-frequency signals to degrade Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs), and proposed Distributional Requery Guard (DRG) to mitigate it.
key_points: ILL uses Sentence Attention Scale Estimation to identify active audio intervals and Frequency Confusion Transfer to build continuous-phase low-frequency waveforms.
Across six LALMs, ILL degraded model accuracy by up to 67 percentage points while remaining effectively inaudible to humans (mean rating of 1.33 vs. 1.17 for clean audio).
To counter low-frequency risks, DRG detects distribution shifts and conditionally prompts for a second recording, recovering mean attacked accuracy from 28.5% to 46.1%.
summary.why_it_matters: It identifies a critical safety vulnerability where inaudible, low-frequency audio signals can severely disrupt LALM performance without alerting human users.

papers.title: CW-BASS v2: Saturation-Aware Pseudo-Label Selection for Semi-Supervised Segmentation under Foundation-Model Teachers

summary.tldr: CW-BASS v2 is a saturation-aware pseudo-label selection method for semi-supervised segmentation that dynamically switches between strict confidence filtering and an adaptive floor based on teacher reliability measured on a held-out slice.
key_points: DINOv2 foundation-model teachers cause confidence saturation (e.g., 98% of Pascal VOC pixels reach confidence >= 0.95), causing adaptive thresholding methods to fail due to confirmation bias.
CW-BASS v2 evaluates teacher reliability on a held-out slice via pi_kept = Pr[correct | c >= tau] using an operating threshold tau not tuned to mIoU.
If the teacher is reliable (pi_kept >= tau), the method applies strict filtering; otherwise, it defaults to a self-adaptive confidence floor that bounds retention away from 1.
CW-BASS v2 matches UniMatch V2 on saturated datasets (87.4 mIoU on Pascal VOC 1/8) and outperforms it by +1.5 mIoU on ADE20K where the teacher's confident set is unreliable.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents pseudo-label filtering failures when using modern self-supervised foundation models as teachers, automatically adapting the filtering strategy without manual tuning across diverse benchmarks.

papers.title: TailBooster: A Dual-Layer Generative Framework for Extreme Value Augmentation with Operational Validity Enforcement

summary.tldr: TailBooster is a model-agnostic, dual-layer generative framework that uses statistical tail extraction and deep learning anomaly filtering to generate operationally valid tabular synthetic data for extreme events.
key_points: Combines an Interquartile Range (IQR) statistical layer to feed tail-concentrated data into a Tabular Variational Autoencoder (TVAE) with an autoencoder-based cleaning layer to filter operationally invalid records.
Addresses under-represented distributional tails and eliminates infeasible mixed-type tabular instances, such as short air times paired with long flight distances.
Reduces Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 47-49% for extreme air time and 29-57% for extreme arrival delay predictions across six regression algorithms compared to conventional synthetic data.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables accurate prediction of rare, high-impact disruptions without needing hardcoded domain-specific rules or sacrificing operational data validity.

papers.title: PixSDS: Why Latent SDS Makes Noisy Pixels

summary.tldr: PixSDS resolves VAE-induced pixel drift and high-frequency noise in latent Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) by using decoded lookahead steps to guide pixel-space gradients without changing the underlying diffusion model or SDS objective.
key_points: Identifies latent SDS failure mode where image-space optimization moves along VAE encoder weak constraints, causing visible pixel noise while latents remain semantically clean.
Introduces PixSDS, a lightweight gradient repair method that decodes a latent SDS lookahead step to provide a clean optimization direction in pixel space.
Eliminates VAE-inconsistent noise and structured color artifacts without requiring diffusion model retraining, renderer modifications, or objective replacements.
Validates effectiveness across controlled 2D SDS experiments, VAE-only optimizations, and text-to-3D generation tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It fixes visual artifacts and high-frequency noise in text-to-3D generation workflows using a lightweight, plug-and-play gradient correction method.

papers.title: Toward a Gricean Retreat: Probing LLMs for Knowledge Boundaries and Referent Specificity

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that while LLM internal activations contain signals for both knowledge boundary awareness and upcoming referent specificity, current generation policies fail to reconcile them to perform a Gricean retreat to safer, generic claims.
key_points: Evaluated LLM behavior using a T-REx-based benchmark that systematically varies entity familiarity and referent specificity.
Probing confirms LLM activations encode both whether an entity is within its knowledge boundary and the specificity level of the referent it is about to generate.
Models consistently generate specific referents for unknown entities, even when accurate generic alternatives are explicitly provided.
The internal substrate for Gricean retreat (trading informativeness for truthfulness) exists within LLM representations, but current decoding policies lack the mechanism to act on it.
summary.why_it_matters: Identifying that knowledge awareness exists in model representations provides a foundation for developing steering or alignment objectives that reduce hallucinations by forcing models to fall back to generic, true statements.

papers.title: Synthetic Persona Pretraining: Alignment from Token Zero

summary.tldr: Synthetic Persona Pretraining (SPP) embeds value-aligned assistant personas from the start of pretraining using normative reflection annotations, improving model alignment and jailbreak robustness after post-training persona binding.
key_points: SPP annotates standard pretraining documents with value-aligned first-person reflections derived from a normative value constitution.
Models up to 3B parameters were pretrained on 500B tokens using standard cross-entropy loss over both original documents and synthetic reflection data.
Post-training user-assistant dialogue data performs 'persona binding', linking the target pretrained persona directly to the assistant identity.
Applying SPP at token zero yields better constitution adherence, stronger jailbreak robustness, and lower misalignment in moral dilemmas compared to applying it late in pretraining.
The alignment advantages of early SPP scale positively with the overall pretraining budget.
summary.why_it_matters: Pretraining-time persona interventions prevent values from acting as a superficial overlay, producing AI models that are inherently resilient to misalignment and jailbreaks without degrading core capabilities.

papers.title: A Unifying Perspective on Causal World Models: From Observations to Representations to Structure

summary.tldr: This paper provides a formal definition of Causal World Models (CWMs) that unifies observational generation, object-centric representations, structural dynamics, and formal identifiability guarantees for causal reasoning and decision-making.
key_points: Formalizes Causal World Models (CWMs) to move beyond simple generative prediction by explicitly capturing entity properties, entity-to-entity, and entity-to-environment interactions.
Connects world modeling tasks to causal representation learning, object-centric learning, causal discovery, and structural causal models (SCMs).
Evaluates CWM components against literature on identifiability to specify the formal conditions and equivalence classes under which environment dynamics can be recovered from data.
summary.why_it_matters: Grounding world models in formal causal representations enables AI agents to reliably predict, plan, and generalize beyond their training distributions.

papers.title: Are You Sure You're Sure? On the Impact of Instruction Tuning on Confidence and Lexical Diversity

summary.tldr: Instruction tuning alters LLM confidence and reduces cross-rationale diversity without significantly improving predictive accuracy, demonstrating that verbalized confidence and rationale diversity capture distinct, persistent effects.
key_points: Evaluated three matched pairs of base and instruction-tuned models on question-answering benchmarks to measure confidence, accuracy, calibration, and diversity.
Instruction tuning consistently shifts verbalized answer confidence despite minimal changes in accuracy and lower likelihood-based calibration.
Cross-rationale diversity decreases consistently after instruction tuning, whereas surface-level lexical diversity varies in direction and magnitude depending on the model and benchmark.
Observed shifts in confidence and diversity persist even after controlling for answer selection and rationale length.
summary.why_it_matters: Instruction tuning can induce model overconfidence and narrower rationale generation without delivering proportional gains in answer accuracy, complicating reliability in question-answering applications.

papers.title: It's How You Ask: Gender-Associated Linguistic Bias in LLMs

summary.tldr: A study reveals LLMs systematically generate shorter, less sophisticated, and less formal responses when prompts use female-associated linguistic features, regardless of explicit gender names.
key_points: Prompts containing hedges, tag questions, and collective references elicited inferior outputs across three document types and four evaluated models.
Linguistic register influenced model responses far more than explicit gender cues like sign-off names, though both map to the same internal representational space.
Mechanistic analysis shows these linguistic features are encoded in early transformer layers and remain entangled with other representational features.
Bias effects persisted even after controlling for prompt complexity and feature carry-over, making post-hoc user mitigation difficult.
summary.why_it_matters: Linguistic bias in LLMs can create disparate impacts in professional workplaces by penalizing communication styles commonly used by women.

papers.title: TsuGO: Probing Search Efficiency in LLM Reasoning via Go Life-and-Death Problems

summary.tldr: TsuGO is a new benchmark that uses Go life-and-death problems to evaluate LLM search efficiency by parsing chain-of-thought outputs into structured search trees.
key_points: TsuGO leverages Go tsumego problems to create closed, verifiable, adversarial solution spaces that force candidate generation, branch comparison, and backtracking.
The framework disentangles domain knowledge from search organization, measuring Search Efficiency alongside Token Efficiency and visual diagnostic metrics.
Experimental findings reveal that stronger LLMs succeed by discovering correct candidates earlier and sustaining focus on productive branches rather than relying on longer chains-of-thought.
Most current LLMs behave similarly to unguided search algorithms rather than neural-guided engines like KataGo, showing that longer CoT does not correlate with better search efficiency.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes search organization and resource allocation as critical, measurable dimensions in LLM reasoning beyond simple final-answer accuracy or CoT token length.

papers.title: GEM: A Generative Embedding Model Bridging Reasoning and Retrieval

summary.tldr: GEM is a generative embedding model that unifies reasoning and retrieval by generating context about query intent and appending an embedding token to represent the enriched context for vector search.
key_points: Combines text generation and vector embedding in a single unified architecture.
Generates explicit reasoning over a query before appending a final embedding token to encode the enriched context.
Outperforms its non-reasoning variants and matches retrieval baselines that rely on significantly larger models.
Supports test-time compute scaling via prompting to improve retrieval accuracy on complex tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: GEM closes the semantic gap between complex user reasoning instructions and traditional dense retrieval models without relying on separate multi-stage pipelines or larger external models.

papers.title: SkillShapley: Boundary-Adaptive Shapley Valuation for Skill Step Attribution in LLM Agents

summary.tldr: SkillShapley is a two-phase framework that uses boundary-adaptive Shapley valuation to estimate the performance contribution of individual steps within LLM agent skills.
key_points: Models skill-step attribution as a Shapley value-based contribution estimation problem to quantify step-level contributions.
Addresses discretized benchmark reward cliffs by first identifying informative coalitional regions.
Exploits additive step interactions by adaptively sampling new coalitions to generate reusable marginal evidence.
Validated on SkillsBench to identify high- and low-value skill steps efficiently.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables developers to automatically identify and refine high- or low-value steps in long procedural agent skills without relying solely on manual evaluation.

papers.title: Intern-S2-Preview: Scientific Agentic Foundation Model

summary.tldr: Intern-S2-Preview is a scientific agentic foundation model series featuring a 397B backbone and unified post-training, optimized for multimodal scientific reasoning, time-series forecasting, and long-horizon agentic tasks.
key_points: Unified post-training pipeline integrates SFT, scalable multi-task RL, black- and white-box agentic RL, and on-policy distillation.
Training stability and efficiency are supported by partial rollouts with off-policy correction, adaptive length regularization, online speculative decoding, and trace-aware experience assembly.
Intern-S2-Preview-397B extends time-series modeling to numerical forecasting on the SciTS benchmark.
The separate Intern-MemDec-4B memory decoder increases Biology-Instructions average scores from 56.92 to 60.32 without altering the frozen 397B backbone.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable scientific discovery by combining long-horizon tool interaction, specialized memory extensions, and multimodal time-series forecasting without retraining massive base models.

papers.title: Neural Quadratic Forms: A Unified Minimal Model for Sudden Learning and Scaling Laws

summary.tldr: A unified mathematical model using symmetry-derived quadratic forms reduces various neural architectures to Lotka-Volterra dynamics, explaining both abrupt step-like learning and smooth power-law scaling during training.
key_points: Symmetry and smoothness enforce a universal leading-order quadratic form, $\Tr[WW^{\top}A(x)]$, for initial near-zero weight expansions, encoding architectural details into a single structure matrix $A(x)$.
Unified architectures including perceptrons, attention, mixtures of experts, and convolutions close their training dynamics on the order parameter $M=WW^{\top}$.
When data matrices share an eigenbasis, learning dynamics reduce to a Lotka-Volterra equation where modes switch on sequentially based on initial weight scale.
The framework demonstrates that sudden plateau drops are a singular limit of smooth flow, while unresolved modes merge to yield predictable power-law scaling in training time.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a single theoretical foundation to predict, compute, and analyze both sudden phase transitions and power-law scaling dynamics across diverse deep learning architectures.

papers.title: A Probe Direction Is a Property of Its Prompt

summary.tldr: Published probe scores for detecting evaluation awareness reflect arbitrary prompt choices rather than model properties, reversing scaling trends and rendering single-prompt model comparisons invalid.
key_points: Single-prompt probe designs cause reported scores and scaling trends to vary by prompt selection, explaining contradictory results in previous literature using a single experimental design.
Variance in reported probe numbers is primarily driven by model-prompt interactions, meaning expanding evaluation items fails to fix measurements while diversifying prompts does.
Standard evaluation-probe dataset splits are largely linearly separable by surface-level text features alone, allowing directions devoid of evaluation information to achieve high scores.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating evaluation-awareness in language models using single-prompt activation probes is unreliable for model benchmarking and requires multi-prompt measurement designs.

papers.title: TRAPSBench: Vision-Language Models Encode but Fail to Express Epistemic Restraint

summary.tldr: The new TRAPSBench benchmark reveals Vision-Language Models internally represent visual unanswerability with up to 0.91 AUROC but fail to express epistemic restraint, achieving a maximum Penalized Epistemic Calibration Score of just 0.292.
key_points: TRAPSBench provides 1,404 procedurally generated paired physics videos to evaluate epistemic abstention under occluded or chaotic visual evidence.
Evaluations across 16 VLMs yielded a top Penalized Epistemic Calibration Score (PECS) of 0.292, with models detecting textual uncertainty 4x better than visual uncertainty.
Linear probes decode unanswerability from internal hidden states at up to 0.91 AUROC across Qwen, Gemma, and LLaVA model families.
Steering a single-layer void direction causally controls model abstention, proving the bottleneck lies in output expression rather than visual perception.
summary.why_it_matters: Improving VLM reliability requires targeted output-stage interventions rather than perceptual upgrades, as models already possess the internal representation needed to refrain from guessing.

papers.title: Explanatory Engagement Under Rare Anomalous Failure: Asymptotic Rarity in Model Behavior (or: The Asymptotic AI)

summary.tldr: Evaluating open-weight LLMs under varying failure probabilities (0.2 to 0.0001) reveals that explanatory engagement under rare anomalies depends heavily on elicitation structure, showing plateaus or unprompted self-monitoring rather than collapse.
key_points: Evaluated qwen3:8b, llama3.1:8b, and mistral:7b on a tool-call task across eight failure probabilities (0.2 to 0.0001) and five elicitation conditions.
Under the immediate_forced condition, explanation length peaks at 28.4 words at p=0.05 and plateaus at 17.4-19.0 words at rarer rates, while confidence increases from ~53% to the 70s-90s.

In passive_unprompted settings, llama3.1:8b independently outputs structured confidence reports that fluctuate as trials accumulate, whereas qwen3:8b and mistral:7b only emit single boilerplate instances.
A companion guaranteed-failure run across 72 cells demonstrated that a model's ability to recognize an anomaly is distinct from its level of engagement once recognized.
summary.why_it_matters: Determining how LLMs report rare system failures helps developers design prompt elicitation workflows that maintain reliable automated error diagnostic behaviors in low-fault environments.

papers.title: From Local Mismatch to Global Impact: Optimizing Cache Reuse Policy for Efficient Diffusion

summary.tldr: GCache optimizes diffusion model cache reuse by formulating policy search as a bilevel optimization problem using a Bernstein-reparameterized error propagation bound.
key_points: Identifies that local similarity heuristics in existing cache policies misalign with final generation quality due to non-uniform error propagation and accumulation.
Derives a theoretical error propagation upper bound and reparameterizes its propagation exponent using a Bernstein form.
Formulates cache policy search via bilevel optimization, finding an optimal reuse policy in the inner objective while aligning error-weighting with quality loss in the outer objective.
Achieves a 2.17x speedup on the Wan2.1 video diffusion model while reducing LPIPS from 0.1095 to 0.0316.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables significantly faster image and video diffusion inference without sacrificing visual quality by replacing naive local cache heuristics with a globally optimized reuse policy.

papers.title: SAEVerbalizer: Generating Explanations for Sparse Autoencoder Features via Representation Verbalization

summary.tldr: SAEVerbalizer fine-tunes an LLM's downstream layers to generate natural-language explanations of Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) features directly by injecting their decoder directions into the model's internal representations.
key_points: SAEVerbalizer eliminates reliance on external behavioral observation by translating SAE decoder directions directly into natural-language explanations.
The fine-tuned verbalization capability generalizes to unseen features, transfers across separate SAE dictionaries, and adapts to SAE features from different LLMs via a lightweight adapter.
Intervention experiments confirm that injecting multiple feature directions combines their meanings, while reversing directions causes corresponding semantic shifts.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly decoding SAE feature directions into text significantly improves the computational efficiency and accuracy of interpreting large language model internal representations at scale.

papers.title: Measuring Task-Agnostic Training Data Influence Across Language Model Pretraining

summary.tldr: A new task-agnostic influence measure quantifies training data influence by measuring how much an example's gradient update reduces the squared distance to a pretraining run's final parameters.
key_points: Defines training influence as the reduction in squared distance to final model parameters caused by an example's gradient update.
Estimates influence directly from intermediate checkpoints without requiring retraining, specific downstream tasks, or validation sets.
Evaluated across 18 model configurations from the Pythia and PolyPythia suites.
Reveals a temporal crossover in influence: literature-related data align more with the trajectory early in training, while STEM data become more influential in later stages.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient, trajectory-level measurement of training data importance across pretraining stages without relying on arbitrarily chosen validation tasks.

papers.title: Beyond Local Accuracy: A Protocol-Level Identifiability Audit for Controlled LLM Reasoning Evaluation

summary.tldr: LLM benchmark scores can be precise even when the observation protocol does not identify the behavioral property they are intended to measure. In a controlled, solver-grounded setting, we formalize a protocol-level ident

papers.title: Refusing Intent, Not Form: Wrapper-Based Intent-Group Supervision for LLM Safety

summary.tldr: Wrapper-Based Intent-Form Augmentation (WIFA) pairs wrapped harmful prompts with matched wrapped benign counterexamples to train models to base refusal decisions on intent rather than surface form shortcuts.
key_points: WIFA generates intent-group augmentations automatically without requiring external teacher models or manual intent labels.
WIFA-Boost uses a two-stage fine-tuning recipe to achieve high transformed-harmful refusal rates on Qwen and Llama models.
Anchored Group-Consistent Refusal Training (A-GCRT) regularizes decision scores across same-intent wrappers and enforces a margin between harmful and benign groups.
A-GCRT reduces OR-Bench over-refusal in the Qwen setting from 25.7% (base model) down to 17.4%.
Ablations confirm that data structure, two-stage training order, and A-GCRT components drive performance improvements over reproduced baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLMs to resist wrapper-based adversarial jailbreaks while simultaneously mitigating over-refusal on complex benign queries without extra annotation costs.

papers.title: TEMPO: Makespan-Aware Expert-Parallel Load Balancing Across Memory- and Compute-Bound Regimes

summary.tldr: TEMPO is a makespan-aware expert-parallel dispatcher that models MoE load using a max-affine profile to account for both memory-bound weight streaming and compute-bound tile padding.
key_points: Identifies two MoE execution regimes split around N* ≈ 156-168 tokens: memory-bound weight streaming below the threshold and tile-padded grouped GEMM compute above it.
Formulates per-batch dispatch as a fixed-charge makespan problem captured by the max-affine execution profile t = max(a + bG, c + βN).
Fuses token dispatch with count collection in a single in-graph kernel integrated out-of-process with SGLang.
Achieves up to 15.5% lower block time in microbenchmarks, 4-6% higher throughput, and ~15.6% lower p99 latency on Qwen3-235B.
summary.why_it_matters: Traditional count-based dispatchers fail when MoE batches mix hot and cold experts, whereas TEMPO's phase diagram accurately models mixed-regime hardware overheads to reduce tail latency.

papers.title: Unifying Depth and Width Pruning for LLMs via Binary Knapsack Optimization

summary.tldr: SNIPER is a two-stage LLM structured pruning framework that unifies depth and width pruning using binary knapsack optimization to achieve exact compression budgets and superior performance retention.
key_points: SNIPER uses a two-stage approach: knapsack optimization over coarse-granularity components based on importance estimates, followed by fine-grained pruning to enforce strict budgets.
Introduces the Compression Ratio Adherence Factor (CRAFT) metric, where SNIPER achieves a 0.98 score compared to existing pruners that deviate from target budgets by up to 33%.
Evaluated across four model architectures and 18 tasks in five domains, achieving a mean performance rank of 1.25 against six state-of-the-art structured pruners.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the budget overshooting and suboptimal parameter allocations typical of greedy pruning heuristics, enabling predictable and optimal LLM compression.

papers.title: Decoupled Contrastive Decoding via Expert-Aligned Drafting

summary.tldr: Decoupled Contrastive Decoding (DCD) accelerates Contrastive Decoding by using an expert-aligned lightweight drafter for speculation and confining the amateur model strictly to the verification stage.
key_points: Diagnostics reveal contrastive-aware drafting underperforms because contrastive corrections are typically smaller than drafter errors, which reconstruction can amplify.
DCD uses standard speculative verification to guarantee that the output distribution matches vanilla Contrastive Decoding.
Using an EAGLE3-based drafter, DCD yields 1.65x to 1.95x average greedy speedups over vanilla CD on 8B models.
DCD cuts MMLU proposal-path latency by 5x to 12x compared to amateur-coupled proposal methods.
summary.why_it_matters: DCD resolves the computational bottleneck of Contrastive Decoding by delivering significant inference speedups without altering the original output distribution.

infra.title: ClusterNetworkPolicy in GKE: Balancing control and autonomy for your microservices

summary.tldr: ClusterNetworkPolicy is a new feature in GKE that provides cluster-wide network security control, enabling administrators to set overarching traffic rules across all namespaces while preserving tenant autonomy.
key_points: Introduces ClusterNetworkPolicy to enforce baseline network security controls across entire GKE clusters.
Allows platform administrators to define cluster-wide security rules without overriding namespace-level NetworkPolicies.
Balances centralized security governance with microservices autonomy for multi-tenant GKE environments.
summary.why_it_matters: Platform teams can enforce mandatory cluster-wide security baselines without breaking developer-managed namespace network configurations.
